name: Rolldown
summary: A JavaScript bundler written in Rust that keeps Rollup’s plugin API at esbuild’s speed; the bundler inside Vite since Vite 8.
intro: Rolldown takes entry files, builds the module graph and writes bundles, like Rollup or esbuild. It accepts the same plugin API as Rollup and Vite, so existing plugins mostly work, and its own benchmarks put it on par with esbuild and 10 to 30 times faster than Rollup. Its feature set is closer to esbuild’s than Rollup’s: TypeScript and JSX transforms, syntax lowering, Node-style module resolution, mixed ES module and CommonJS graphs, `define` and minification are built in rather than added through plugins. Parsing, transforming, resolving and minifying are done by Oxc.

It was built so that Vite could drop its two bundlers (esbuild in development, Rollup in production) for one, and it has been Vite’s default bundler since Vite 8 (March 2026). It also works on its own: `npx rolldown -c` reads a `rolldown.config.js`. Version 1.0 (May 2026) froze the public API under semantic versioning. Because plugins written in JavaScript run outside the Rust core, Rolldown adds hook filters, which let a plugin declare which files it cares about so the bundler skips the call into JavaScript for everything else.
strengths: esbuild-class speed with Rollup’s plugin API; early adopters of the Rolldown-powered Vite reported production builds 3 to 16 times faster
Batteries included: TypeScript, JSX, CommonJS interop and Node-style resolution need no plugins
Fine control over chunks with webpack-style `codeSplitting` groups, the feature behind Framer’s 67% cut in chunk count
Shares Oxc with Vite’s other tools, so parsing and transforms behave the same across the stack
limits: Output details (dead-code elimination, chunking and inlining heuristics, option defaults) may still change within 1.x; only the API is frozen
JavaScript plugins pay for each hop from Rust into JavaScript; plugins without hook filters slow the build down as you add them
Some features are still experimental, such as watch mode, native MagicString and lazy barrel optimization
Doesn’t polyfill Node.js built-ins for the browser; that needs a separate plugin

story: Vite started with two bundlers: esbuild, written in Go, for speed in development, and Rollup, written in JavaScript, for its plugin API and careful production output. The pair worked, but it meant two transformation pipelines, two plugin systems and glue code to keep them aligned, and esbuild couldn’t be customised enough to take over everything. Evan You and the Vite team decided to build one bundler with Rollup’s API and esbuild’s speed, written in Rust.

Rolldown was open-sourced in 2024, its first public release (0.10.1) coming in April, and in October Evan You founded VoidZero, which holds the project’s copyright and funds a full-time team, to finish it together with the Oxc compiler it is built on. In May 2025 a `rolldown-vite` package let people try it as a drop-in replacement for Vite; GitLab cut a build from 2.5 minutes to 40 seconds and Excalidraw from 22.9 to 1.4 seconds. Vite 8’s beta made it the default in December 2025, Vite 8 shipped in March 2026, and Rolldown reached 1.0 in May 2026 with about 200 contributors.

choices.choice: The whole pipeline in Rust, not Rust pieces inside a JavaScript bundler
choices.why: Moving parts of a JavaScript tool to Rust often loses the gain to the cost of passing data between the two, as Rollup 4 found with its Rust parser. Parse, transform and code generation all stay native and run in parallel.
Vite’s whole plugin ecosystem was written against it. Without compatibility, every Vite user would have had to rewrite plugins to upgrade.

choices.choice: Build on Oxc and parse each file once
choices.why: Vite sometimes parsed the same TypeScript file five times at different layers of the stack. Sharing one parser and syntax tree removes repeated parsing and lets AST work such as emitting type declarations run in parallel during bundling.

Calling into JavaScript for every file is the main cost of a JS plugin in a native bundler. A plugin that declares an `id`, `code` or `moduleType` filter is skipped entirely for files that don’t match.

timeline.text: VoidZero founded in October to fund Rolldown and Oxc; 1.0 beta in December
Vite 8 beta makes Rolldown the default bundler in December
VoidZero joins Cloudflare in June; Rolldown stays MIT-licensed
